questions.q: Do Receiving and Payables post journal entries directly to the General Ledger?
options: Yes, both subledgers write directly to the GL with no intermediate step
No, Subledger Accounting takes each subledger's accounting events and creates the journals that are transferred to the General Ledger
No, only Payables can post to GL; Receiving never produces accounting
Yes, but only once per fiscal year
questions.explain: Subledger Accounting (SLA) is the engine that translates subledger events into balanced journals before they reach the General Ledger.

questions.q: What does the receipt accrual journal from lesson 18 do, as it travels toward the GL?
options: Debits accounts payable and credits cash
Debits cash and credits the supplier's bank account
Debits the maintenance expense account and credits the uninvoiced receipts accrual account
Has no accounting impact at all
questions.explain: The receipt accrual journal, originating in Receipt Accounting, debits the expense account and credits the uninvoiced receipts accrual liability.

questions.q: What does drilling down from a GL journal line let a consultant do?
options: Nothing useful - GL journals cannot be traced back to their source
Change the chart of accounts structure
Automatically approve the original requisition
Trace the journal backward through Subledger Accounting to the specific source transaction, such as the invoice, receipt, purchase order, and requisition
questions.explain: Drill-down lets a consultant trace a GL amount back to its originating subledger transaction and, from there, back through the whole document chain.

questions.q: What produces the third and final journal in this transaction's accounting?
options: The actual cash payment disbursed through the Payment Process Request, debiting accounts payable and crediting cash
Dana submitting her original requisition
Priya's receipt being created
Marcus approving the purchase order
questions.explain: The payment itself produces the final journal, clearing the accounts payable liability by debiting it and crediting cash.

questions.q: Where does the maintenance expense from this transaction ultimately appear on LTV's financial statements?
options: On the balance sheet as a long-term asset
Only on a supplier's own financial statements, never LTV's
It never appears on any financial statement
On the income statement, within the cost structure for the manufacturing plant
questions.explain: The expense account rolls up into LTV's income statement as part of the plant's cost structure, while the liability affects the balance sheet until paid.
